name: Skyline Divide Route

pitch_detail.notes: Trailhead through forest to Skyline Divide meadows (Trail #678), ~2 miles
Along Skyline Divide ridge crest to ~6,563 ft, ~2.5 miles of established trail
Cross-country south along the ridge to the Chowder Ridge junction
Chowder Ridge traverse on an established boot-path; mild exposure, side-hilling on steep slope
Final northwest-ridge summit block; loose rock, hard class 3 scrambling to the small, exposed summit

descent_text: From the summit, carefully downclimb the short Class 3 step and the loose scree/talus below it back to the base of the summit block. Retrace the boot-packed path along Chowder Ridge and the open ridge crest (roughly 3 miles) back to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft), then descend the maintained Skyline Divide Trail #678 through meadows and forest switchbacks to the trailhead.
approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. FS 37 has been closed by the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1, and during the repair work it is gated near its start (mile 0.03), so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle; check the road's status before planning around it. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows on the ridge crest (~2 mi), follow the crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft, ~4.5 mi), then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.
overview: The more popular of Hadley Peak's two standard approaches, following the well-known Skyline Divide trail up onto the ridge crest and then continuing cross-country along Chowder Ridge to the base of Hadley's summit block for a long, scenic ridge-walk scramble.
beta: From the Skyline Divide Trailhead, a rugged, eroded trail switchbacks through forest to the ridge crest at about 2 miles, then rolls over a series of knolls along the open crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft) at about 4.5 miles. From there the maintained tread fades into a boot-packed path that continues along the open ridge crest for roughly another 3 miles, crossing minor ups and downs on Chowder Ridge, before reaching the base of Hadley Peak's final scramble. The last push is Class 2 with a short Class 3 step, climbing loose scree and talus to the summit; exposure is generally minimal for experienced parties.
face: Northwest Ridge (Chowder Ridge - Hadley Peak connecting ridge)
